tldr: Pommerman is a multi-agent benchmark environment based on Bomberman designed to advance research in general-sum, N-player multi-agent learning, addressing the lack of suitable benchmarks beyond two-player zero-sum games.
contributions: Introduction of Pommerman as an open-source multi-agent environment with cooperative and competitive variants
Hosting of competitions including an FFA competition and a NIPS 2018 competition track event
Demonstration that the environment is challenging for standard RL algorithms and requires novel strategies
Provision of a symbolic, low-dimensional state representation to reduce computational barriers for research
methods: The authors designed Pommerman as an 11x11 grid-based game with at least four agents, featuring team and Free-For-All variants with mechanics including bomb placement, destructible wooden walls, power-ups, and optional communication channels. They tested standard RL algorithms (Deep Q-Learning and Proximal Policy Optimization) against a baseline SimpleAgent, evaluated DAgger for behavioral cloning bootstrapping, and hosted community competitions with Docker-based agent submissions.
results: Over 500 people joined the Discord server and more than half of repository commits were from open source contributors. Multiple published papers used Pommerman. DQN and PPO failed to learn successfully without very large batch sizes and shaped rewards. DAgger achieved FFA win rates at or above the SimpleAgent baseline of approximately 20%. In the FFA competition, Yichen Gong's Finite State Machine Tree-Search agent won 22 of 35 matches, while Görög Márton's agent won 8 of 35. Agents discovered a novel bomb-kicking strategy not attempted by novice humans.
limitations: A local optimum exists where agents learn to never use the bomb action to avoid self-destruction, which is ineffective since bombs are necessary to win. Standard RL algorithms out of the box struggle significantly, requiring large batch sizes and shaped rewards. The environment strips away sensor input (no pixel observations), making it less apt for robotics research. The game has few mathematical guarantees for N-player learning.
